title: Delhi HC: A Pagdi Claim Cannot by Itself Defeat a Bona Fide Eviction
case_name: Md. Kamruddin v. Devi Dayal Saini
citation: RC.REV. 334/2025, decided 3 November 2026 (uploaded 6 November 2026), Harish Vaidyanathan Shankar, J.
card_summary: The Delhi High Court dismissed a tenant's revision and upheld an order evicting him from a shop in Masjid Moth. The tenant said a pagdi payment explained his low rent, but did not dispute the landlord's title or the tenancy itself. The court held that this went only to the rent amount, not the landlord's bona fide need, citing Section 5(2)(a) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, which bars a pagdi over rent.
card_tip: Raising a pagdi payment in an eviction case does not, by itself, stop a landlord's bona fide need claim; the tenant still has to show no reasonably suitable alternative accommodation is available to the landlord.
